core_obligations: Check the properties of the functor (proof lines 6835-6836): for a monomorphism f : X -> Y the induced functor (Sch/X)_tau -> (Sch/Y)_tau is continuous, cocontinuous and fully faithful, the last because a monomorphism of schemes induces an injective pullback on the big sites.

Apply the criterion (proof lines 6836-6837): for such a functor the cited same-chapter-free result of the chapter Sites gives that the canonical map f_big^{-1}f_{big,*}F -> F is an isomorphism for every sheaf F on (Sch/X)_tau.
Conclude (proof line 6837): this is the statement.
proof_roadmap: For a monomorphism f, the induced functor on the big sites is fully faithful.
It is also continuous and cocontinuous, since it comes from a morphism of schemes.
Apply the criterion identifying the adjunction unit as an isomorphism for such functors.
Read off the statement for f_big.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a monomorphism f : X -> Y the canonical map f_big^{-1}f_{big,*}F -> F is an isomorphism for sheaves on the big site of X (statement lines 6824-6832). The proof checks the three properties required by the cited criterion: the induced functor (Sch/X)_tau -> (Sch/Y)_tau is continuous and cocontinuous because it comes from a morphism of schemes, and fully faithful because f is a monomorphism (proof lines 6835-6836), after which the criterion in the chapter Sites yields the conclusion (proof lines 6836-6837). The content is the reduction of a geometric hypothesis, being a monomorphism, to full faithfulness of the induced functor. The claim is H2: one reduction and one cited criterion.
